Subject: Post-call recap: quantization tradeoffs & next steps

Thanks again for a great call earlier - quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned.

TL;DR
- Recommended shortlist: Mistral-Instruct-7B (AWQ 4-bit), Llama-2-13B (GPTQ 4-bit), Falcon-40B (FP16/FP8 experiment)
- Next step: run a 48-72 hour eval of those variants on your prompt set (attached) to measure top-line quality + throughput tradeoffs
- Redwood can spin up a dedicated trial environment and run the trade study; Neha can lead the technical setup.

Call highlights
- FinWave's main goals: reduce per-token inference cost while keeping < 1% QA regression on your core NLU prompts; target latency p50 < 200ms for interactive flows.
- Workload: ~70% short text classification & slot extraction, 30% generation for templated responses. Average prompt length 120 tokens, response length ~60 tokens.

Recommended evaluation plan
1) Baseline: Llama-2-13B FP16 (current reference)
2) AWQ (Mistral-Instruct-7B) - likely best cost/throughput tradeoff for short prompts; expect ~1.7-2.2x token throughput vs FP16 with small quality delta on instruction tasks
3) GPTQ (Llama-2-13B 4-bit) - more conservative quality profile, slightly lower throughput vs AWQ but closer to baseline quality
4) FP8 experiment (Falcon-40B FP8-compatible runtime) - highest throughput upside (~2.5-3x) but requires stability checks; good for high-throughput batch paths

Attachments and artifacts
- eval_promptset_finwave.csv (your prompt set, redacted) - please double-check labels for the slot-extraction rows.
- quantization_tradeoffs_v1.pdf - high-level trade study we ran on comparable workloads (numbers are indicative).

What we need from you
- Confirm the prompt set in the attached CSV and flag any privacy/PII rows to exclude.
- Confirm the target SLA (latency/cost) and whether you want us to prioritize conversational latency vs batch throughput.

Proposed next steps
- Neha to provision Dedicated trial and run 48-72h trade study on the attached prompt set (no production data required).
- Follow-up sync (30 min) next week to review results and pick the model/quantization config for canary rollout.

Happy to schedule - available Mon/Tue afternoon PT.

Best,

Hi all - quick technical note on expected numbers (derived from our internal benchmarks on similar short-instruction workloads). These are approximations and we should validate on FinWave's prompt set.

Summary (avg per-token throughput vs baseline Llama-2-13B FP16)
- AWQ (Mistral-Instruct-7B, 4-bit AWQ): ~1.8-2.1x throughput; expected slot-extraction F1 drop ~0.3-0.9% absolute on our evals for comparable prompts
- GPTQ (Llama-2-13B, 4-bit GPTQ): ~1.5-1.8x throughput; F1 drop ~0.1-0.5% absolute - generally safer for sensitive NLU tasks
- FP8 (Falcon-40B, FP8 runtime): ~2.3-2.8x throughput on GPU families that support efficient FP8 kernels; quality impact varies more, sometimes better on generative fluency but more brittle on extraction tasks

Latency (p50/p95) for 120-token prompt / 60-token response (estimates)
- Baseline (Llama-2-13B FP16): p50 ~140ms, p95 ~320ms
- AWQ (Mistral-7B): p50 ~85-110ms, p95 ~210-260ms
- GPTQ (Llama-2-13B 4-bit): p50 ~100-130ms, p95 ~240-300ms
- FP8 (Falcon-40B): p50 ~60-90ms (depending on kernel maturity), p95 can spike if kernels fallback to slower paths

Notes and recommendations
- For FinWave's extraction-heavy workload, GPTQ on Llama-2-13B is the conservative starting point (least quality regression). If cost is the dominant driver and small F1 deltas are acceptable, AWQ on Mistral gives the best cost/throughput without large regressions for instruction tasks.
- FP8 is attractive for batch-heavy pipelines and high-throughput async paths - we should run careful stability checks before using it for interactive flows.
- We recommend running the eval across 3 configs in parallel (baseline + AWQ + GPTQ) for 48 hours; if FinWave wants FP8 explored, add a 4th experiment but note it needs slightly more engineering oversight.

Operational notes
- Redwood trial infra: we can provision a dedicated pool for the run (we'll isolate the trial and provide logs). Typical setup time: 4-6 hours to provision + ingest prompt set. Compute charge will be applied to the trial estimate in HubSpot (we'll share expected cost).
- Deliverables: per-config latency distributions, token throughput, F1/accuracy by task, sample failure cases, recommended canary rollout plan.

I can run the setup if you confirm the prompt set and we have a short window for X-headers (no production PII).

- Neha
